regimes.name: 1929 at the entry year
regimes.anchor: Anchored on fed_history_1929: Dow 381.17 on 3 Sep 1929 to 41.22 on 8 Jul 1932, 89% below the peak; the 1929 high was not regained until 23 Nov 1954.

regimes.name: 2008 at the entry year
regimes.anchor: Anchored on fed_history_2008: S&P 500 -57% from the October 2007 peak to the March 2009 trough; house prices about -30% mid-2006 to mid-2009.

regimes.name: Persistent 6% inflation

paths.name: Live in it
paths.desc: The heir occupies the house. It cannot be let. Their own housing is the return.

paths.name: Let it out
paths.desc: Kept as a rental. No principal-residence exclusion is available on a later sale.

paths.name: Sell at the transfer
paths.desc: Sold in the year of inheritance. The stepped-up basis means little or no gain.

paths.name: Live in it, then sell
paths.desc: Occupied for the first years (securing the exclusion and the 121 gain exclusion), then sold. This is the only holding path that gets both reliefs.

paths.name: Let it, then sell
paths.desc: Let from the transfer, sold later. Rent now, exclusion lost.

paths.name: Sell, park in Treasuries, phase in
paths.desc: Sold at the transfer; proceeds parked in 3-month to 2-year Treasuries for 24-36 months, then moved into equities in equal monthly tranches.

paths.name: Live, then sell, parked, phased in
paths.desc: Occupied first, sold, then the 24-36 month Treasury park and phased entry.

paths.name: Let, then sell, parked, phased in
paths.desc: Let first, sold, then the Treasury park and phased entry.

gaps.F01: Property A's tax rate area, and therefore its published total ad valorem rate. The county's per-area table was not read because the area is unknown. The model uses the county's verified floor (its 1% maximum levy plus its 0.0388% retirement levy) to an assumed 1.40% ceiling.
gaps.F02: No independent appraisal, no comparable sales, no rental comparables for either property. Rents here are a yield range applied to the modelling base, not a market rent.
gaps.F03: No binding insurance quote for either property. Premiums are an assumed range.
gaps.F04: The parcel tax on the three-unit building: the official ballot text and the certified result were not confirmed from an official source in this session. It is a parameter, and the page shows the size at which it would change the answer.
gaps.F05: The city documentary transfer tax rate for the jurisdiction of property B: the city's published rate page returned 'Page Not Found' at the address tried. The rate is a range.
gaps.F06: Article XIII A itself was not opened; its 1% levy and 2% cap are taken from the county's own compilation, which quotes both.
gaps.F07: No official Treasury yield was retrieved this session. The Treasury rate is an assumed range.
gaps.F08: The inflation record is the repository's earlier transcription of BLS CUUR0000SA0, not a fresh retrieval.
gaps.F09: California's marginal schedule and its treatment of long-term gain were not confirmed from the Franchise Tax Board booklet. Only the statutory 1% above $1,000,000 is applied.
gaps.F10: That California has no estate or inheritance tax was not confirmed from an official state page; no figure here depends on it, because the estate is modelled against the federal exclusion only.
gaps.F11: The 27.5-year straight-line depreciation period and the 70% building share are assumptions.
gaps.F12: Whether the trust or the heir is the transferor under RTC 63.2, and how the resident exemption applies to a trust, were not resolved from an official source.
gaps.F13: Prior publication of household figures cannot be undone by editing this repository. See privacy/.
gaps.F15: Housing symmetry is an assumption: the heir lives either in property A or in the vacant unit at property B, so no path charges the heir market rent. If the heir would live elsewhere and pay rent, add that cost to the live, let and sell paths alike.
gaps.F14: Local rental rules for the three-unit building (rent-increase limits, just-cause, short-term-rental limits, the treatment of an owner-occupied unit) were not verified from the city's ordinance.

timeline.what: Title moves to the heir (or the trust continues to hold it). The date fixes the value for the federal estate and the new basis.
timeline.rule: RTC 63.2 treats a transfer by death as a transfer, whether or not it is in a trust.

timeline.what: The heir must occupy, and file the homeowners' or disabled veterans' exemption.
timeline.rule: RTC 63.2(a)(1)(A) and (B): both limbs are conditions of the exclusion.

timeline.what: File the intergenerational transfer exclusion claim with the county assessor, sooner if the house is sold.
timeline.rule: RTC 63.2(b): no exclusion unless a claim is filed; the claim itself is not a public document (RTC 63.2(c)).

timeline.when: Within six months of a supplemental or escape notice
timeline.what: A late claim is still timely if filed in this window.
File Form 706 above the filing threshold, or to elect portability.
timeline.rule: IRS: nine months, with an automatic six-month extension on Form 4768.

timeline.what: The intergenerational value cap is adjusted for the FHFA California house price index.
If the heir stops occupying, the exclusion ends and the base year value is re-enrolled at the next lien date.
First and second secured property-tax instalments become delinquent.
timeline.rule: County compilation: a 10% penalty, then 1.5% a month from 1 July.

timeline.what: Re-read the federal exclusion, the cap adjustment, the local rate area and the two policy questions (parcel tax, city transfer tax).
timeline.rule: This desk carries each one forward and marks it.
